title: Outfit Repeat Confidence Window
dataSources: Wardrobe items (`wardrobe:item`), outfit wears (`outfit:wear`), skincare routines (`skincare:routine`), laundry cycles (`laundry:cycle`).
app: Wardrobe and grooming logs — closet apps (Whering, Stylebook), cost-per-wear trackers, skincare-routine logs, and smart-laundry cycles — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=outfit:wear
| sort 0 person outfit_id _time
| streamstats current=f last(_time) as previous_wear by person outfit_id
| eval days_between=round((_time-previous_wear)/86400,1)
| stats avg(days_between) as avg_repeat_gap by person outfit_id
| sort - avg_repeat_gap
description: Calculates how many days typically pass before you repeat the same outfit combination.
value: Some people want more outfit rotation, others want fewer decision points; repeat-gap data supports either strategy.
implementation: Use `outfit_id` in wear logs and measure average days between repeats with `streamstats`.
visualization: Table of outfits with average repeat gap.
grandmaExplanation: It maps how long you usually wait before wearing the same outfit again.
